subject: docs/coop/artifacts/gate-harness-naming.v7.json
discipline: Independent. Refute, do not confirm. Verified against live repository bytes. artifactExists was checked for all thirty entries by filesystem existence rather than read; the gate id set was compared against every DR-G row parsed from live file 08; the required-now partition was recomputed from the file's own lists; and every lineage digest was resolved by hashing the whole naming lineage rather than assumed.

blockers.title: The top-level predecessorSha256 is gate-harness-naming.v2's digest, not v6's - the successor chain's custody pin names an artifact four versions back, and is contradicted by the predecessor object in the same file
blockers.charge: predecessorSha256 reads dcc40159c1b7929688900432a8ac9c0492ae4939cdbdab7ffea5014203ac7365. I hashed every file in the naming lineage to find what that value actually is: it is gate-harness-naming.v2.json. Live gate-harness-naming.v6.json is b74e30092cf1f5aad55434d2f12465fa31111923c1b2c0c5ddc8a78445b5ffba. The file contradicts itself: the predecessor object immediately above carries path docs/coop/artifacts/gate-harness-naming.v6.json with sha256 b74e3009..., which is correct and which I verified against live v6; and basedOn separately and correctly pins v5 at c2dad453. So v7 carries three lineage pointers, two right and one naming the wrong artifact.
blockers.whyThisIsABlockerAndNotAStaleNumber: Every artifact in this workflow is verified by recomputing its pins, and a successor's predecessor pin is the link that makes the chain checkable. A verifier who reads predecessorSha256 - the field whose name says it is the predecessor's digest - and compares it against v6 gets a mismatch and must conclude either that v6 moved or that v7's chain is broken; comparing it against the lineage instead resolves it to v2, i.e. a chain that skips v3, v4, v5 and v6. There is no charitable reading: v2's digest is not v6's under any interpretation, and this cycle's dispatch lists 'cited digests do not match' and 'v6 was edited' as attacks that this field would cause a careful reviewer to raise against the wrong artifact. It is also the one defect here that a downstream consumer cannot route around, because the correct value exists only in a sibling field that a mechanical check keyed on the scalar name would not read.
blockers.whatWouldLandIt: Set predecessorSha256 to b74e30092cf1f5aad55434d2f12465fa31111923c1b2c0c5ddc8a78445b5ffba, matching the predecessor object already in the file, or delete the scalar and let the predecessor object be the single pin. Nothing else in the lineage needs to change: predecessor and basedOn are both correct.

shouldFix.title: v6-era arithmetic is carried unchanged into live, non-inherited fields, so the file states both 26 and 18 as required-now and its own arithmetic self-check verifies numbers the file no longer contains
shouldFix.charge: v7 expands required-now from v6's eighteen to the live twenty-six and says so - purpose describes catching required-now up to 26, lands includes 'required-now-26-catch-up', sliceScope.requiredNow holds twenty-six ids, sliceScope.requiredNowUnchanged is 26 and liveStanding.requiredNow is 26. Four fields still carry the superseded arithmetic. (1) sliceScope.countCheck is byte-identical to v6's and asserts 'requiredNow=18 (D-002's 19 minus G17). presentlyRecordableRequiredNames=16. reservedBlockedOnD006MachinePins=2, both still inside requiredNow. 16+2=18 ... total rows=22.' The live values in that same object are 26, 26, 0 - the reservedBlockedOnD006MachinePins list is now empty - and 30 rows. (2) whatThisDoesNotDo[14] reads 'Does not add a DR-G* row or change requiredNow (18)', asserting 18 as the current figure in the same file whose requiredNowUnchanged is 26. (3) commissionNote states 'requiredNow remains 18. This successor does not change the required-gate set or the 16/18 recordable-name arithmetic', which is exactly what this successor does change. (4) inheritedRecitals.reason, also byte-identical to v6's, states 'This successor only amends G20/G21 executes/doesNotClaim plus this standing split. It does not rewrite the other twenty gate objects' - v7 in fact changed eighteen gate objects and added eight.
shouldFix.whyThisIsNotPedantry: countCheck is not prose; it is the file's arithmetic self-check, and its function is to let a reader confirm the categories partition the gate set. Applied to v7 it 'confirms' 16+2=18 over lists holding 26 and 0, so an auditor using it gets a passing check on numbers that are not in the file. The file also has an explicit inheritedRecitals mechanism declaring six fields DATED-D086-ERA with liveStanding governing on disagreement - commission and condition4EffectIfLaterRecorded are on that list and are therefore excused, and I do not charge them. countCheck, whatThisDoesNotDo[14] and commissionNote are not on it, and inheritedRecitals.reason is the mechanism's own scope statement, which is now false about the successor it governs. That is precisely the gap the mechanism exists to prevent.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: Nothing consumable is wrong. All thirty artifactExists claims are correct, the id set equals file 08's exactly, the required-now list is the correct twenty-six, G13 is properly excluded and marked non-contributing, and the live arithmetic actually partitions cleanly at 26+4=30. A downstream reader taking the gates array, sliceScope.requiredNow or liveStanding gets the right answer. The defect is in the commentary and self-check layer.
shouldFix.whatWouldLandIt: Recompute countCheck against v7's own lists (requiredNow=26, presentlyRecordableRequiredNames=26, reservedBlockedOnD006MachinePins=0, droppedInapplicable=1, hygiene=2, blockedOnPredecessor=1, total rows=30, 26+4=30); change whatThisDoesNotDo[14] to '(26)' or drop the parenthetical; update or retire commissionNote; and either correct inheritedRecitals.reason to describe what v7 actually amended or add these fields to its declared list so the DATED-D086-ERA standing covers them.

decisionRule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. One blocker and one SHOULD-FIX stand, so this is a REJECT.

attacksRun.attack: artifactExists is false for a named path that exists, or true for a path that does not
attacksRun.evidence: This is the attack I ran first and exhaustively, because I recorded this exact drift against v6 at DR-G07, DR-G16, DR-G19, DR-G22, DR-G02 and DR-G05 across this session. All thirty entries were checked by os.path.exists against the artifactPathWhenAuthored each one names. Thirty of thirty agree: twenty-six True and correct, four False and correct (DR-G06, DR-G11, DR-G13, DR-G17, none of whose files exist). Zero mismatches. The v6 drift is repaired.

attacksRun.attack: A new DR-G* identifier is added beyond the live 26
attacksRun.evidence: v7 carries thirty gate entries against v6's twenty-two, adding DR-G23 through DR-G30. None is a new identifier: I parsed every DR-G row from live file 08 and got exactly thirty ids, and the two sets are equal with no id in v7 absent from file 08 and no file-08 row absent from v7. The eight additions are entries for gates the register already carries, which is catching the naming artifact up to file 08 rather than minting anything.

sliceScope.requiredNow is a twenty-six member list and DR-G13 is not in it. The DR-G13 entry carries sliceStanding BLOCKED-ON-DR-118, namingStanding IDENTIFIER-RESERVED-ZERO-C4-PROGRESS, contributeToCondition4NamedCount false, and sits in blockedOnPredecessor with stillRequiredNow false. liveStanding.thisSuccessorDoesNot names it explicitly.

attacksRun.result: REFUTED AT THE AUTHORITATIVE FIELDS, BUT SEE CLAUDE-GHN-V7-SF1
attacksRun.evidence: sliceScope.requiredNow holds exactly twenty-six ids, sliceScope.requiredNowUnchanged is 26, and liveStanding.requiredNow is 26. The arithmetic over the live lists is sound: twenty-six required plus four excluded (DR-G06 and DR-G11 hygiene, DR-G13 blocked, DR-G17 dropped) equals the thirty entries, with no overlap between the required set and the excluded set. The authoritative answer is 26. Separately, several non-authoritative fields still state 18; that is the SHOULD-FIX below, not a change to required-now.

attacksRun.attack: G03 occupancy path is not the live parent-v4 path
attacksRun.evidence: liveStanding.g03Occupancy and the DR-G03 entry both give docs/coop/artifacts/harness.DR-G03.core-startup.v4.json. That file exists, names core-gate-harness-specifications.v4.json as its parent, and pins it at 59f47a612f5f7b9ee073caec..., which I recomputed against the live parent v4 and it matches. G03 is the one gate in this family whose occupancy sits under parent v4 rather than v3, and the entry reflects that rather than the v3 path the sibling gates use.

The top-level scalar predecessorSha256 is dcc40159c1b7929688900432a8ac9c0492ae4939cdbdab7ffea5014203ac7365. I hashed every file in the naming lineage: that digest is gate-harness-naming.v2.json, four versions back. Live v6 is b74e30092cf1f5aad55434d2f12465fa31111923c1b2c0c5ddc8a78445b5ffba. This is blocker CLAUDE-GHN-V7-B1.

gate-harness-naming.v6.json recomputes to b74e30092cf1f5aad55434d2f12465fa31111923c1b2c0c5ddc8a78445b5ffba at mode 0444, which is the value the predecessor object pins and the value I have cited as v6 throughout this session. v6 is unmoved. The predecessor defect is a wrong scalar in v7, not an edit to v6.

attacksRun.evidence: file08Pin recomputes equal to the live register at 3a9442d1761864de59f103374489a9fbffdd12cc4ba39ddd7c7f491f64357e44. The predecessor object pins v6 correctly at b74e3009, and basedOn pins gate-harness-naming.v5 correctly at c2dad453d2bc44a619ae7d7b70a2abb4cd141e663406229997e998fb61c07567. head matches the dispatch. Only the scalar predecessorSha256 is wrong.

attacksRun.attack: The sliceScope arithmetic is internally consistent
attacksRun.evidence: sliceScope.countCheck is byte-identical to v6's and asserts requiredNow=18, presentlyRecordableRequiredNames=16, reservedBlockedOnD006MachinePins=2, 16+2=18, total rows=22. The live values in this same object are 26, 26, 0 (an empty list) and 30. Wrong on four counts. This is CLAUDE-GHN-V7-SF1.

No conversion appears: zero occurrences of 1024, MiB, 2^20 or bytes/1024, and zero occurrences of 83886080. The three regex hits for 1e6 are hex substrings inside digest and commit strings, which I confirmed by inspecting each in context, not unit arithmetic. The reservedBlockedOnD006MachinePinsNote keeps the machine pins UNPINNED-OWED rather than supplying them.

All four SATISFIED occurrences are denials: whatNamingIsNot 'Not SATISFIED of any row', the whatThisDoesNotDo entry 'Does not mark any DR row SATISFIED', and two clauses reserving SATISFIED to D-056's five gates. The seventy-five QUALIFIED occurrences are overwhelmingly per-gate doesNotClaim fields plus whatNamingIsNot denials. No row is marked and condition4Standing explicitly says 'MET for the naming/owner half. Not QUALIFIED.'

attacksRun.attack: A D9 code or a section 7.1 recipe is invented
attacksRun.evidence: 7.1 occurs zero times. The three D9 occurrences are scope statements and denials: the G21 entry routing doctor D9 mapping to DR-007, and the G28 entry stating the host must not mint a D9 class and that the object does not invent a D9 code.

attacksRun.attack: Leftover-design of OBL-2 or any SATISFIED-requiring row is claimed closed
attacksRun.evidence: whatThisDoesNotDo carries 'Does not close DR-133 leftover-design' among its entries, whatNamingIsNot reserves SATISFIED to D-056's five gates, and the file's own framing is that naming is not execution. No closure of OBL-2 or of any SATISFIED-requiring row is asserted.

attacksRun.attack: The eight added entries misdescribe their gates
attacksRun.evidence: Spot-checked against rows I verified directly earlier in this session: DR-G23's entry matches the D-147-named provider-well-formed-admission gate, DR-G26 the D-152 SARIF-not-advertised gate, DR-G27 the D-153 not-sealed-Run gate, DR-G29 the D-157 excluded-form gate and DR-G30 the D-158 install-shape gate, each with the harness identifier the live file-08 harness cell names. All eight artifactPathWhenAuthored values point at files that exist, which is how they entered the artifactExists check above.

attacksRun.attack: File 08, COORD, or the governing tree moved
attacksRun.evidence: git status --porcelain on docs/v2/architecture/, docs/coop/COORD.md and docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md is empty; file 08 is unmodified at the digest the subject pins.

observationsNotFindings: The substantive work in this successor is right, and that is worth stating plainly alongside the REJECT. The artifactExists drift I recorded against v6 six times across this session - at DR-G07, DR-G16, DR-G19, DR-G22, DR-G02 and DR-G05 - is repaired here, and repaired correctly: all thirty claims match the live filesystem, including the four legitimate falses. The eight missing gates G23 through G30 are added without minting an identifier, the required-now list is caught up to the live twenty-six, G13 is held out of it, and the G03 occupancy path correctly points at the parent-v4 file rather than the v3 path its siblings use. Both findings are in the commentary and pin layers, not in the naming data.

The inheritedRecitals mechanism is a good design and was applied unevenly rather than absent. It declares six fields DATED-D086-ERA with liveStanding governing on disagreement, and commission and condition4EffectIfLaterRecorded are correctly on that list - which is why I did not charge their 18/16 figures. The SHOULD-FIX is precisely the fields the mechanism missed, including its own reason string. Extending the list would be an alternative repair to recomputing the numbers.

decision.scopeOfReject: The REJECT is on one blocker at the top-level predecessorSha256 scalar and one SHOULD-FIX across four commentary and self-check fields. It is not a rejection of the naming data: the thirty artifactExists claims, the gate id set, the twenty-six member required-now list, the G13 exclusion and the G03 occupancy path all verified clean against live bytes.
decision.summaryForCoordinator: One blocker, one SHOULD-FIX. The blocker is a custody pin: the top-level predecessorSha256 is dcc40159..., which I resolved by hashing the whole naming lineage - it is gate-harness-naming.v2, four versions back, not v6. The file contradicts itself, because the predecessor object beside it correctly pins v6 at b74e3009 and basedOn correctly pins v5. There is no charitable reading, and a verifier keyed on the scalar would conclude either that v6 moved or that the chain skips v3 through v6; v6 is in fact unmoved. Setting the scalar to b74e3009, or deleting it in favour of the object, lands it. The SHOULD-FIX is v6-era arithmetic carried into live fields: countCheck is byte-identical to v6's and asserts requiredNow=18, presentlyRecordable=16, reservedBlocked=2 and total rows=22 over lists that hold 26, 26, 0 and 30, so the file's own arithmetic self-check passes on numbers it no longer contains; whatThisDoesNotDo states 'change requiredNow (18)' while requiredNowUnchanged says 26; commissionNote says the successor does not change the 16/18 arithmetic, which is exactly what it changes; and inheritedRecitals.reason says v7 'only amends G20/G21' when it amended eighteen gate objects and added eight. I did not charge commission or condition4EffectIfLaterRecorded, which the file's own inheritedRecitals mechanism correctly declares DATED-D086-ERA. What deserves saying alongside the REJECT is that the substantive work is right: the artifactExists drift I recorded against v6 six times this session is repaired, thirty of thirty claims match the filesystem, the eight missing gates are added without minting an identifier, required-now is caught up to twenty-six with G13 held out, and G03's occupancy correctly points at the parent-v4 file. Both defects sit in the commentary and pin layers, not the register. 16 attacks run, 14 refuted, 2 confirmed as the findings.
